chains.title: No TF-mediated effect at this variant
predictions: In relevant glioblastoma cells, the variant will not produce a reproducible allele-specific binding effect for the candidate TFs or a TF-dependent change in TERT expression; any disease association could reflect linkage or another process.
falsified_if: An allele-specific assay shows a reproducible binding difference at this base and a corresponding TF-dependent change in TERT expression.

chains.title: Speculative MAX-mediated effect at the TERT promoter

links.claim: The testable prediction is that MAX binds alt A more strongly than ref G, but the supplied evidence gives no allele-specific binding direction or QBiC-SELEX result; MAX is a candidate because it is expressed and has more site-overlapping peaks in other biosamples than the other named candidates, not because its occupancy in glioblastoma is established.
The variant lies in a promoter-like cCRE with active chromatin marks reported across ENCODE biosamples, although activity in glioblastoma is not established.
The variant is annotated upstream of TERT and at its transcription start site, but this positional evidence does not demonstrate that the cCRE regulates TERT.
Glioblastoma is the supplied expression context, but no matching-biosample MAX occupancy evidence is reported.

A TERT regulatory effect could be relevant to glioblastoma, where TERT promoter mutations are common, but these sources do not establish a MAX-mediated effect of this variant or a disease effect in this case.

predictions: Compared with ref G, alt A will show greater MAX binding in a relevant assay; if this chain is correct, perturbing MAX will alter the allele-dependent effect on TERT expression, though the direction of the expression change is not established.
falsified_if: A sufficiently sensitive allele-specific assay finds no greater MAX binding to alt A.
MAX perturbation does not alter any allele-dependent effect on TERT expression in relevant cells.

checks.why: A site-overlapping MAX peak in a relevant glioblastoma biosample would materially strengthen the cell-context link; its absence would further weaken it.

matrix.test: Compare ref G and alt A probes in an electrophoretic mobility-shift assay using glioblastoma nuclear extract, with MAX- and JUN-specific supershift or depletion controls.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-specific MAX- or JUN-containing complex.
A MAX-containing complex binds the alt A probe more strongly than the ref G probe.
A JUN-containing complex binds the ref G probe more strongly than the alt A probe.

matrix.test: In a glioblastoma model, compare allele-specific MAX and JUN occupancy and TERT expression after editing the variant; perturb the candidate TF to test whether any expression effect depends on it.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-specific occupancy or TF-dependent TERT-expression effect.
Greater MAX occupancy on alt A and an allele-dependent TERT-expression effect that changes with MAX perturbation; the expression direction is not specified.
Greater JUN occupancy on ref G and an allele-dependent TERT-expression effect that changes with JUN perturbation; the expression direction is not specified.

next_experiment: Run the low-cost allele-specific EMSA with glioblastoma nuclear extract and MAX/JUN supershift or depletion controls. It directly tests the predicted MAX binding difference separating the two highest-probability chains, while also checking the JUN alternative; a positive binding result would still need follow-up to establish an effect on TERT expression.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.

Conclusions: Understanding both telomere-dependent and -independent TERT functions is essential for developing effective biomarkers and therapies that overcome resistance and slow melanoma progression.
The genetic landscape of familial melanoma is heterogeneous.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
Mutations in the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter region (TPM), particularly C228T and C250T, are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM).

The rs[masked] C allele may increase GBM susceptibility and, when in cis with TPM, is associated with reduced TERT expression and poorer prognosis, underscoring its biological and clinical significance in TPM-mutant GBM.
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.
The prognostic relevance of CDKN2A deletion may vary according to TERTp status, particularly for OS.
